kill_reasons.reason: Free open-source capture tools (ArchiveBox, Browsertrix) already cover the technical wedge at $0 and the rule names no required vendor, so willingness to pay $29/mo depends entirely on convenience and trust for non-technical RIAs, which is unevidenced.

The social half depends on platform terms that conflict with the product promise: Meta requires App Review for third-party apps and requires deleting Platform Data when no longer needed or when the operator stops operating the product, against a 5-year retention promise by a solo operator.
Email and written communications must be archived as well (Rule 204-2(a)(7)), so the buyer needs a full archiving tool anyway and a web/social-only product is at best an add-on second vendor.
Buyer pool is the SEC-registered subset (starts at $100M AUM); smaller advisers are state-registered and follow state rules that were not checked.
The adviser carries the safeguard duty for electronic records, so vendor 'compliant' claims create liability and the entrant may only describe capture features.

legal_notes: 17 CFR 275.204-2(a)(11)(i)(A) and (e)(1): an SEC-registered adviser must keep a copy of each advertisement it disseminates for at least 5 years in an easily accessible place; 204-2(g)(3)(i): the adviser must keep procedures to safeguard electronic records from loss, alteration or destruction.
17 CFR 275.206(4)-1(e)(1): an advertisement is any direct or indirect communication to more than one person that offers advisory services, so website and social posts are in scope.
Do not claim the product is SEC- or 17a-4-compliant or exam-proof; describe only capture, timestamping and export features. Whether a legal review would allow stronger claims was not assessed.
Meta Platform Terms: App Review for third-party apps; delete Platform Data when no longer needed or when the product stops operating; LinkedIn, X and Instagram terms were not readable.
State-registered advisers (below $100M AUM) are governed by state books-and-records rules, which were not read.
metadata.verdict_reason: Mandatory need is verified (Rule 204-2: keep a copy of each advertisement for 5 years), but the pages that decide the idea (Patrina, Smarsh, Archive Intel pricing, social platform ToS) could not be re-fetched and search budget ran out. Free OSS (ArchiveBox, Browsertrix) covers capture at $0, Meta terms force deletion of platform data, and email must be archived anyway, so a $29 web/social-only add-on has no verified edge. Year-1 profit ~+$25, pessimistic ~-$2.7k. Leaning kill; not provable on verified evidence.
